# How do I ...?

<!-- Generated by (write-manual! DIR) in scheme/packages/howto.scm. Do not edit: change the source and run bin/docs. -->

Each section is one task. Inside the editor, `C-h h` asks for a task and opens its page. The keys here are the stock keys.

## Getting started

### How do I run a command by its name?

Press `M-x` (`execute-extended-command`) and type a part of the name. The list gets shorter as you type. Each row shows the key of the command and what the command does. Press `RET` to run the selected command.

Every action in the editor is a command. When you forget a key, you can always use its name.

To search by what a command does, use `s-p` (`command-palette`). It also finds task recipes.

### How do I cancel what I started?

Press `C-g` (`keyboard-quit`). It closes a prompt, stops a key sequence, and clears the mark. Press it again if one press is not enough.

### How do I undo a change?

Press `C-/` (`undo`). Each press takes back one more change. The editor keeps the undo history of each buffer.

### How do I learn the editor step by step?

Press `C-h t` (`help-with-tutorial`). The tutorial is a buffer that you edit while you read it. The editor keeps your place when you leave, and the tutorial opens there next time.

`M-x setup-welcome` shows the short version on one page.

### How do I find out what a key does?

Press `C-h k` (`describe-key`), then press the key. A page opens. It names the command, says what the command does, and says which keymap binds the key.

`C-h b` (`describe-bindings`) lists every key that works in this buffer. `C-h m` (`describe-mode`) shows the keys of this buffer's mode only.

### How do I get help about what is here?

Press `M-?` (`contextual-help`). The page describes the name at point, this buffer, its mode, and its keys.

In a list (buffers, files, chats, mail), press `?` to show the keys of the list.

### How do I find the name of something?

Press `C-h a` (`apropos`) and type some words. The page lists the commands, settings, functions, and recipes that match. Click a name to open its source.

## Files

### How do I open a file?

Press `C-x C-f` (`find-file`) and type a path. The list shows the files in the directory as you type. Press `RET` to open the selected file. A new path makes a new buffer, and `C-x C-s` (`save-buffer`) writes it to disk.

`C-x 4 f` (`find-file-other-window`) opens the file in the other window.

### How do I save a file?

Press `C-x C-s` (`save-buffer`). To save the buffer under a new name, use `C-x C-w` (`write-file`).

When the file changed on disk after you opened it, the editor asks before it writes. `M-x revert-buffer` reads the file from disk again and discards your edits.

### How do I browse a directory?

Press `C-x C-d` (`dired`) and choose a directory. Dired lists its files.

- `RET` (`dired-visit`) opens the file at point.
- `^` (`dired-up`) opens the parent directory.
- `R` (`dired-rename`) renames or moves a file.
- `C` (`dired-copy`) copies a file.
- `+` (`dired-mkdir`) makes a directory.
- `m` (`list-mark`) marks a file. A command then acts on every marked file.

### How do I find a file in my project?

Press `C-x p f` (`project-find-file`) and type a part of the name. The list holds the files of the project that git does not ignore.

A project is a directory under version control. `C-x p p` (`project-switch-project`) goes to another project.

### How do I search the text of my project?

Press `C-x p g` (`project-ripgrep`) and type the text. The list shows each match. Move through the list to preview a match, and press `RET` to go to it.

### How do I mark a place to come back to?

Press `C-x r m` (`bookmark-set`) and give the bookmark a name. `C-x r b` (`bookmark-jump`) goes back to it later, also after a restart. `M-x bookmark-bmenu-list` lists every bookmark.

## Editing

### How do I select, cut, copy, and paste?

Press `C-SPC` (`set-mark-command`) to start a selection, then move point. The region is the text between the mark and point.

- `C-w` (`kill-region`) cuts the region.
- `M-w` (`copy-region-as-kill`) copies the region.
- `C-k` (`kill-line`) cuts from point to the end of the line.
- `C-y` (`yank`) pastes the last text you cut or copied.
- `M-y` (`yank-pop`), after a paste, replaces it with the text you cut before that.

### How do I search in a buffer?

Press `C-s` (`isearch-forward`) and type. Point moves to the next match as you type. Press the same key again for the next match. Press `RET` to stop at the match, or `C-g` (`keyboard-quit`) to go back to where you started.

`C-r` (`isearch-backward`) searches toward the start of the buffer.

### How do I replace text?

Press `M-%` (`query-replace`). Type the text to find, then the new text. At each match, press `y` to replace it or `n` to skip it.

`M-x replace-string` replaces every match with no questions.

### How do I go to a line?

Press `M-g g` (`goto-line`) and type the line number.

`M-<` (`beginning-of-buffer`) goes to the start, and `M->` (`end-of-buffer`) goes to the end. `M-g i` (`imenu`) goes to a definition in this buffer by its name.

### How do I make the text larger or smaller?

Press `C-+` (`text-scale-increase`) or `C-_` (`text-scale-decrease`). The change applies to this buffer only. `s-)` (`text-scale-reset`) gives the buffer the normal size again.

## Buffers and windows

### How do I switch to another buffer?

Press `C-x b` (`ibuffer-prompt`) and type a part of the buffer name. Press `RET` to show it.

`S-<left>` (`previous-buffer`) goes back to the buffer you used before. `C-x C-b` (`ibuffer`) lists every buffer by group.

### How do I close a buffer?

Press `C-x k` (`kill-buffer`) and choose the buffer. The current buffer is the default. When the buffer has unsaved changes, the editor asks first.

### How do I split the screen?

Press `C-x 3` (`split-window-right`) for two windows side by side, or `C-x 2` (`split-window-below`) for one above the other.

- `C-x o` (`other-window`) moves to the next window.
- `C-x 0` (`delete-window`) closes this window. The buffer stays open.
- `C-x 1` (`delete-other-windows`) keeps this window only.
- `C-x l` (`window-layout`) arranges the visible buffers in a layout that you choose.

### How do I get back the windows I had?

Press `C-c <left>` (`winner-previous`). Each press restores an earlier arrangement of windows and buffers. `C-c <right>` (`winner-next`) goes forward again.

### How do I read the other window without leaving this one?

Press `C-M-v` (`scroll-other-window`) to scroll the other window down, and `M-<up>` (`scroll-other-window-down`) to scroll it up. Point stays in this window.

## Groups

### How do I keep the buffers of one task together?

A group is the set of buffers for one task, with the window arrangement you left. Press `C-x C-g n` (`group-new`) to make a group and enter it. The files you open while you are in a group go into that group.

`C-c g` (`group-add`) puts the current buffer in a group. `C-x C-g m` (`group-move`) moves it to another group.

### How do I switch to another task?

Press `C-x g` (`group-switch`) and choose a group. The editor shows its buffers in the windows you left them in.

`C-x C-g C-g` (`group-switch-last`) goes back to the group you came from.

### How do I rename or close a group?

Press `M-x group-rename` to give the current group a new name. `M-x group-kill` kills every buffer in the current group.

## Agents and chat

### How do I ask the agent about my work?

Press `C-c c` (`chat`). The chat of the current group opens. Type your question after the prompt and press `RET` (`agent-send`).

The agent can read the buffers of the group, so you do not paste them. `C-c RET` (`chat-companion-ask`) asks the chat without leaving the buffer you are in.

### How do I start a new chat?

Press `C-c n` (`chat-new`). With a prefix argument, it asks which group the chat belongs to.

`C-x C-c` (`chat-list`) lists every chat, and finds a chat by a word that somebody said in it.

### How do I give the agent a part of a file?

Select the text, then press `C-c r` (`chat-send-region`). The chat gets the region as context.

### How do I stop the agent?

In the chat, press `C-g` (`chat-abort`). The reply in progress stops, and the transcript keeps what arrived.

`M-x chat-reset` clears the transcript and starts again.

### How do I choose the model?

In a chat, press `C-c m` (`chat-set-model`) to choose the model of that chat. `C-c b` (`llm-configure`) opens the complete setup: backend, model, effort, and saved presets.

`M-x chat-set-permission-mode` changes when the agent asks before it acts. `M-x chat-cost` shows what the chat has cost.

### How do I answer the agent when it asks for permission?

When the agent wants to use a tool, the chat asks you.

- `C-c C-y` (`agent-permission-allow`) allows it once.
- `C-c C-a` (`agent-permission-always`) allows it and stops asking for that tool.
- `C-c C-n` (`agent-permission-deny`) refuses.

## Web, mail, and feeds

### How do I read a web page?

Press `M-x browse` and type a URL or some search words. The page opens as readable text in a buffer.

- `RET` (`browse-follow`) follows the link at point.
- `n` (`browse-next-link`) moves to the next link.
- `l` (`browse-back`) goes back.
- `o` (`browse-open-external`) opens the page in your real browser.

`M-x browse-history` lists every page you read.

### How do I read my mail?

Press `M-x notmuch` to see the mailboxes, or `M-x mail` for the three-pane view. The mail comes from notmuch, so notmuch must index it first.

In the mail list, `a` (`notmuch-archive`) archives a thread, and `r` (`notmuch-reply`) replies.

### How do I follow a news feed?

Press `M-x feeds-subscribe` and give a feed URL or a page that has one. `M-x feeds` lists the new items of every feed.

## Customizing

### How do I change a setting?

Press `M-x customize` and choose the setting. Type the new value. The editor saves it in `~/.compos/custom.scm`, so it stays after a restart.

`M-x customize-set-variable` changes a setting for this session only.

### How do I change the colours?

Press `M-x load-theme`. Move through the list to preview each theme. Press `RET` to keep one.

### How do I bind a key to a command?

Press `M-x keys-bind`, choose the command, then type the key, for example `C-c z`. The binding applies everywhere and stays after a restart.

`C-h B` (`keys`) lists every key. In that list, `b` (`keys-rebind`) gives the command on the row another key, and `u` (`keys-revert`) takes back your edit.

### How do I add my own code?

Put Scheme in `~/.compos/init.scm`. The editor runs it at each start, after the bundled packages.

To try an expression now, press `M-:` (`eval-expression`). In a Scheme buffer, `C-x C-e` (`eval-last-sexp`) runs the expression before point. `M-x reload-file` loads a changed package into the running editor.

## Setup and sharing

### How do I set up the AI models?

Press `M-x setup-ai-guide`. It explains models, chats, and agents, then walks through a real reply. `M-x setup-inference` detects local commands and registered keys; it cannot check a login. For a guided OpenRouter key setup, use `M-x setup-bot`.

### How do I share a link to a buffer?

Press `C-c l` (`copy-buffer-link`). The link names this buffer and this line. A person who opens it gets the editor at that place.

### How do I restart the editor?

Press `M-x restart-daemon`. The editor saves your buffers, windows, and groups, then restarts. They come back after the restart.

A change to a Scheme or Elixir source file does not need a restart: the editor reloads it when you save it.

### How do I see what the editor said?

Press `C-h e` (`view-messages`). The buffer lists every message that the echo area showed, with errors first in their colour.
